$comment: The single source of truth for which runtimes CI exercises.
COMPATIBILITY.md section 7 says: 'A runtime is supported when CI exercises it.'
That sentence is only true if three things agree, so scripts/check-runtime-matrix.mjs
makes them agree mechanically:
1. this file, which .github/workflows/ci.yml expands into job matrices;
2. each package manifest's declared floor (engines.node, requires-python,
the go directive, rust-version, maven.compiler.release, require.php,
TargetFrameworks, environment.sdk, required_ruby_version, the elixir
requirement) — the lowest version tested MUST equal the floor claimed;
3. the table in SUPPORT.md, which is generated from this file.
Raising a floor is a MINOR change (VERSIONING.md). Adding a newer runtime is
a MINOR change. Neither may be done here alone: the manifest and this file
move together, or CI fails.
'stable' entries track the ecosystem's current release. They are the reason a
newly published Go or Rust or Dart version cannot break users silently; the
numeric entry alongside is the floor, and it is the one that is contractual.
HOW THE FLOORS BELOW WERE CHOSEN (reviewed 2026-07-27).
One rule, applied to every runtime: the floor is the oldest version still
expected to receive upstream security fixes roughly twelve months from now.
Twelve months rather than 'today' because a floor that expires between two
releases makes this file claim support the upstream has already withdrawn --
the failure mode is an adopter reading SUPPORT.md and concluding a runtime is
safe when nobody is patching it. Bumping a floor is MINOR (VERSIONING.md);
the whole set is re-derived at each review rather than drifting one entry at
a time.
Two runtimes are not governed by an upstream EOL calendar and are named here
so the choice is not mistaken for one:
rust  1.85 is the edition-2024 release. There is no Rust EOL; the binding
constraint is the dependency graph, which stopped resolving under the
old 1.70 MSRV when serde_json pulled in zmij (needs rustc 1.71+).
1.85 is comfortably below current stable and above that floor.
dart  3.9.0 has no upstream EOL either. It is the oldest SDK the current
lints and test packages still resolve against.
ELIXIR IS TWO AXES, AND THEY MOVE INDEPENDENTLY. The Elixir floor follows the
rule above (1.18). The OTP floor does NOT: OTP 25 is where
:crypto.hash_equals/2 appears ([N-31]), so 25 is a fact about what the code
can run on, and packages/elixir/mix.exs raises below it. Testing a higher
lowest-OTP would leave that guard unexercised and claim less than the package
delivers, so the floor leg pairs 1.18 with OTP 25 deliberately.
